stanzas: עַל יַד בֶּן יִשַׁי בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי
Come, my beloved, to meet the bride;
let us welcome the face of the Sabbath.
the one God made us hear;
the Lord is one and his name is one,
for renown and for glory and for praise.
To meet the Sabbath come, let us go,
for she is the source of blessing;
from the beginning, from of old, she was set up [?];
last in deed, first in thought.
Sanctuary of the King, royal city,
rise, go out from the overthrow;
long enough have you sat in the valley of weeping,
and he will have compassion on you.
Shake yourself from the dust, rise;
put on the garments of your glory, my people;
by the hand of the son of Jesse the Bethlehemite
draw near to my soul, redeem it.
for your light has come; rise, shine;
the glory of the Lord is revealed upon you.
You shall not be ashamed nor be disgraced;
why are you cast down, and why do you moan?
In you the poor of my people will take refuge,
and the city will be rebuilt on its mound.
Those who plunder you shall become plunder,
and all who would swallow you shall be far away;
your God shall rejoice over you
as a bridegroom rejoices over a bride.
Right and left you shall spread out,
and the Lord you shall revere;
by the hand of a man, a son of Perez,
and we shall rejoice and be glad.
Come in peace, crown of her husband,
with joy and with gladness too,
among the faithful of the treasured people;
come, O bride; come, O bride;
al yad ben yishai bet hallakhmi

notes: The divine name is written יְיָ, an abbreviation read "Adonai" ("the Lord"); it is romanized as it is said.
line 2.1: the two forms of the Sabbath commandment, "Keep" (Deuteronomy 5:12) and "Remember" (Exodus 20:8), said by tradition to have been spoken at once.
line 3.3: 'nesukhah' echoes Proverbs 8:23 (Wisdom 'set up' or 'anointed' from of old); the sense is disputed.
line 5.3 and 9.3: the son of Jesse (David) and the son of Perez (David's ancestor) stand for the Messiah.
line 10.4-5: written כַלָּה without dagesh after a vowel, hence khallah.
